description: Dispatch an async job that creates and/or updates up to 300 lead records in one batch, and return {job_id, status} in milliseconds; poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished results, row_count and tallies. action is one of createOrUpdate (default), createOnly, updateOnly, createDuplicate; lookup_field names the dedupe field (defaults to email). The batch shape is checked at dispatch; then, in the background job and before writing, the plugin makes one lead-describe call and refuses the whole batch if any intended non-key field is marked REST read-only. The refusal names every offending field and the records carrying it, and no write is attempted. To preserve read-modify-write, fields in Adobe's documented six-field default Get Leads response are excluded from refusal only when this instance's describe marks them read-only. The literal set has documented, not measured provenance and does not assert read-only membership. Those echoes remain in the outbound record: if a caller genuinely intends to write one, Marketo may silently drop it while returning status updated and no reasons. On an accepted vendor response, inspect every results entry: status may be skipped with a reasons[] array. One unrecognized field name discards that entire record, including valid fields beside it. tallies counts statuses but cannot identify which records were skipped or why. Write action.
embedding_description: Write new leads into Marketo or update existing lead field values in a batch of up to 300 records using the Sync Lead API. Preflight Marketo field metadata once per batch and refuse intended REST read-only write targets before mutation, naming every offending field and record. Use createOnly to insert, updateOnly to modify, or createOrUpdate to upsert by lookup_field.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with job_id (pass to check_marketo_job_status) and status 'queued'. The completed job result is a dict with results (Marketo's vendor-verbatim per-record array: id, status [created/updated/skipped], reasons on skip), row_count, and tallies (a status -> count summary).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: A queued job is not vendor success: give the job_id and poll check_marketo_job_status. Once completed: lead field data is business-contact PII (data_sensitivity 0.3, generic-SaaS floor). Summarize the tallies (e.g. '12 created, 3 updated, 1 skipped'), then inspect every results entry and surface each skipped record's reasons. Never treat tallies alone as proof that every record applied.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Never report created/updated counts from THIS verb's response -- it carries only the job handle. They appear once check_marketo_job_status reports status=completed.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validate a lead batch and dispatch a background job that creates/updates it in the configured Marketo instance.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: Refused at dispatch, before any vendor call and with no job created: marketo.invalid_params for missing/empty records, more than 300 records, an invalid action or lookup_field, or missing session_id/flow_id in the calling context. Reported later in check_marketo_job_status's error field: marketo.invalid_params from the preflight refusal because one or more intended non-key fields are REST read-only. A read-only refusal happens before the write and names every offending field plus the records carrying it. Fields in Adobe's documented default Get Leads response are excluded from that refusal only when this instance marks them read-only; the exclusion prevents echoed read output from bricking read-modify-write but is not evidence that an intended write applied. marketo.not_configured: no marketo_instance address-book entry. marketo.validation_failed: the whole batch was structurally rejected (rare — most per-record failures land in results, not this error). A top-level success can still contain status skipped with reasons[]; Marketo code 1006 means an unrecognized field name caused the entire record to be discarded, including its valid fields. tallies alone does not expose which record failed or why. marketo.auth_failed: OAuth credentials rejected. marketo.permission_denied: the API user's Role lacks Read-Write Person — this write permission is NOT checked by check_setup (unverifiable without performing a write), so this may be the FIRST signal of the gap. A transport fault after dispatch may follow a vendor mutation.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: marketo.invalid_params: remove every read-only field named by the refusal, or fix the action/lookup_field/record shape, then retry. The effective lookup key and a bare id are treated as identifiers rather than write targets. For read-modify-write, strip unchanged default Get Leads echoes where practical. If a caller genuinely intended to change a default field that the instance marks read-only, Marketo may silently drop it while reporting status updated and no reasons; treat that field as vendor-controlled and do not infer application from tallies. Inspect status and reasons[] on every vendor results entry. For a skipped record with code 1006, fix every unrecognized field name and resend that record because none of its valid fields applied; do not infer success from tallies. marketo.permission_denied: add 'Read-Write Person' under Admin > Users & Roles > Roles > <the API role> > Access API, then retry. After a transport fault, read the leads back with get_leads before resending.
